problem.claim: The work asks whether Memory Mosaics retain their compositional and in-context learning properties when scaled to large language-model sizes and real-world datasets.

contributions.claim: Scales Memory Mosaics to 10B parameters and trains them on one trillion tokens.
Introduces architectural modifications called Memory Mosaics v2.
Evaluates training-knowledge storage, new-knowledge storage, and in-context learning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish this work by demonstrating favorable Memory Mosaic properties at 10B scale on real-world data, alongside Memory Mosaics v2 modifications.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that Memory Mosaics v2 match transformers on training-knowledge learning and significantly outperform them on new-task execution at inference time and in-context learning.
The authors report that increasing transformer training data alone does not easily reproduce these improvements.
The authors report that a Memory Mosaics v2 model trained on one trillion tokens performs better on these tasks than a transformer trained on eight trillion tokens.

narrative_sequence.summary: Memory Mosaics had shown compositional and in-context learning capabilities at medium scale and on synthetic small datasets.
The work scales them to 10B size, trains on one trillion tokens, adds v2 architectural modifications, and defines three evaluation dimensions.
The authors report parity with transformers for training knowledge but stronger new-task and in-context performance, including against a transformer trained on eight trillion tokens.
The authors report that simply adding transformer training data does not easily replicate the improvements.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates evaluation into training-knowledge storage, new-knowledge storage, and in-context learning, then reports different comparison outcomes across those dimensions.

lessons.interpretation: Dimension-specific evaluation can reveal where a method differs rather than collapsing capabilities into one aggregate result.
lessons.application: When presenting a new architecture, partition evaluation by knowledge already learned, knowledge acquired after training, and inference-time task adaptation, and report comparisons for each.
lessons.exception: This partition may be unsuitable when the target application has only one clearly defined capability or when the dimensions cannot be operationalized independently.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the v2 architectural modifications, datasets, metrics, model sizes beyond the stated scales, or statistical details behind “significantly.”
The eight-trillion-token comparison may involve other unspecified training or model conditions; the abstract does not establish equivalence beyond token count.
